headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: transaction broker has no duty to conduct independent investigation of buyer's financial condition.

headings.title: Showing alternative properties and competing listings permitted
headings.reviewNote: Corrected note count to 4 subdivisions (not 3). Verified sub 6(1)-(4): may show alternative properties, list competing properties, show same property to competing buyers/tenants, and act as agent/dual agent/subagent in other transactions.

headings.title: Actual knowledge standard and no imputation of information
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 7: parties, transaction broker, and entity personnel are considered to possess only actual knowledge; no imputation by operation of law.

headings.title: Cooperation with other brokers without creating agency
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 8: transaction broker may cooperate with other brokers without establishing agency or subagency.

headings.title: Authority to act as single agent, dual agent, or subagent with disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 9: does not prohibit acting as single limited agent, dual agent, or subagent if disclosure requirements are met.

headings.title: Designated broker vicarious responsibility for affiliated licensees
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 10: does not alter or eliminate broker responsibility for conduct of licensees operating under the broker's license.

headings.title: Compliance with statutory requirements and fair housing laws
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 11(1)-(2): must comply with §§ 339.710–339.860, § 339.010(2), rules, and federal/state/local fair housing and civil rights laws.

headings.title: Right of licensee refusing transaction brokerage to become designated or dual agent
headings.reviewNote: Refined title to include dual agent option. Verified sub 12: licensee refusing transaction broker status to continue agency with both parties may become designated agent or dual agent under §§ 339.730–339.860.

headings.title: Withdrawal from representation upon client refusal to convert relationship
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 13: licensee may withdraw without liability from a client refusing conversion to transaction brokerage without prejudicing representation of the other client or other transactions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.755 (bid 18212), all thirteen subsections with all subdivisions, and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998, A.L. 1999, effective 1-01-00). Corrected subdivision counts in notes for subs 2, 3, and 6; refined sub 12 title to include dual agent option.

headings.title: Residential broker disclosure form requirement at first substantial contact
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: in residential transactions, licensee must provide commission-prescribed broker disclosure form at earliest practicable opportunity during/after first substantial contact with unrepresented party.

headings.title: Exemption from disclosure when written agreement already exists
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: no other licensee need make § 339.770 disclosures when party already has a written services agreement with a designated broker.

headings.title: Legal sufficiency of statutory brokerage disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: disclosures made under §§ 339.710–339.860 are sufficient as a matter of law to disclose brokerage relationships to the public.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.770 (bid 18214), all three subsections, and history notes (L. 1996 through A.L. 2002 H.B. 1964). Retained all three titles.

headings.title: Designated broker execution of brokerage agreements and written authorization
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: designated broker enters written brokerage agreements on behalf of broker and affiliates, or may authorize affiliates in writing to do so.

headings.title: Mandatory terms of written seller or landlord agency agreements
headings.reviewNote: Corrected note (specifies offer of subagency, not dual agency consent). Verified sub 2: written agreement required before § 339.010 acts, including § 339.730 duties, compensation terms, and whether subagency may be offered.

headings.title: Mandatory terms of written buyer or tenant agency agreements
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: written agreement required before non-ministerial § 339.010 acts as single agent for buyer/tenant, including § 339.740 duties and compensation terms.

headings.title: Mandatory terms of written dual agency agreements
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: written agreement with both parties required before § 339.010 acts as dual agent, including § 339.750 duties and compensation terms.

headings.title: Mandatory terms of written subagency agreements
headings.reviewNote: Updated note to include unilateral subagency offers. Verified sub 5: written agreement with client's designated broker before § 339.010 acts, or entry by customer disclosure after a unilateral subagency offer or § 339.820 exclusion.

headings.title: Written transaction brokerage agreement required for compensation
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 6: designated broker acting as transaction broker expecting compensation must enter written agreement with § 339.755 duties and compensation terms.

headings.title: Minimum service requirements in exclusive brokerage agreements
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 7(1)-(3): exclusive brokerage agreements must specify accepting/presenting offers, assisting with offers/counteroffers/notices until signing and contingencies resolved, and answering related questions.

headings.title: Additional contractual duties permitted by agreement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 8: nothing prohibits written contracts with brokers containing duties, obligations, or responsibilities beyond those specified in § 339.780.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.780 (bid 57474), all eight subsections with subdivisions (1)-(3), and history notes (L. 1996 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 595 & 343 merged with H.B. 596). Corrected sub 2 reviewNote ('offer of subagency', not 'dual agency consent') and sub 5 reviewNote (unilateral offer of subagency and excluded-affiliate disclosure); retained all eight titles.

headings.title: Commencement and duration of brokerage relationships
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: relationships commence on the effective date of the broker's agreement and continue until performance, completion, termination, or expiration.

headings.title: Post-termination duties limited to accounting and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2(1)-(2)(a)-(d): no post-termination duties except timely accounting and client confidentiality (with four exceptions: written consent, legal requirement, public disclosure, or defense against wrongful-conduct action).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.790 (bid 18216), both subsections with subdivisions (1)-(2)(a)-(d), and source/effective-date notes (L. 1996 S.B. 664 § 9, effective 9-01-97). Retained both titles.

headings.title: Compensation sources and fee sharing between designated brokers
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: designated broker compensation may be paid by seller, landlord, buyer, tenant, third party, or shared between designated brokers.

headings.title: Payment of compensation does not establish agency relationship
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: payment of compensation alone does not establish an agency or transaction brokerage relationship.

headings.title: Seller or landlord consent to share compensation with other brokers
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: seller or landlord may agree that a designated broker may share compensation with another designated broker.

headings.title: Buyer or tenant consent to share compensation with other brokers
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: buyer or tenant may agree that a designated broker may share compensation with another designated broker.

headings.title: Compensation from multiple parties permitted with full disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: designated broker may be compensated by more than one party with knowledge of all parties at or before entering a written contract to buy, sell, or lease.

headings.title: Written brokerage agreement required for compensation
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 6: section does not relieve licensee of obtaining a written brokerage services agreement or other written compensation agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.800 (bid 18217), all six subsections, and history notes (L. 1996 through A.L. 2004 H.B. 985). Retained all six titles.

headings.title: Client liability for misrepresentation of limited agent or subagent
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: client not liable for misrepresentation of limited agent or subagent unless client knew or should have known.

headings.title: Client liability for misrepresentation of transaction broker
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: client not liable for misrepresentation of transaction broker unless client has actual knowledge.

headings.title: Licensee liability for misrepresentation of client
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: limited agent or subagent not liable for client misrepresentation unless licensee knew or should have known.

headings.title: Limited agent liability for misrepresentation of subagent or affiliate
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: limited agent not liable for subagent or affiliated licensee misrepresentation unless limited agent knew or should have known.

headings.title: Subagent liability for misrepresentation of limited agent
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: subagent not liable for limited agent misrepresentation unless subagent knew or should have known.

headings.title: Transaction broker liability for misrepresentation of client
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 6: transaction broker not liable for client misrepresentation unless transaction broker had actual knowledge.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.810 (bid 18218), all six subsections, and history/effective-date notes (L. 1996, A.L. 1998, effective 1-01-99). Retained all six titles.

headings.title: Appointment of designated agents or designated transaction brokers
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to include designated transaction brokers. Verified sub 1: designated broker may appoint in writing affiliated licensees as designated agents or designated transaction brokers to the exclusion of other affiliates; unrepresented party assisted by affiliate is presumed transaction brokerage.

headings.title: Designated broker not deemed dual agent by appointment
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: designated broker is not a dual agent or transaction broker solely by making an appointment, unless personally representing both parties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.820 (bid 18219), both subsections, and history/effective-date notes (L. 1996 through A.L. 1999, effective 1-01-00). Revised sub 1 title to include designated transaction brokers as well as designated agents.

headings.title: Designated agent and transaction broker duties to clients and customers
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: designated agents and designated transaction brokers have the same §§ 339.730–339.755 duties as the designated broker except as provided in § 339.820.

headings.title: Equal vicarious liability protections for affiliated licensees
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: all licensees have the same vicarious liability protections under §§ 339.710–339.860 as their designated broker.

headings.title: Effective date of January 1, 2000

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 339.830 (bid 18220), all three subsections, and history/effective-date notes (L. 1996 through A.L. 1999, effective 1-01-00). Retained all three titles.
